question.problem: Given the curve $r(t)=⟨\frac{2{t}^{3}}{3},{t}^{2},\,\,t⟩$ for $t>0$, use the cross product curvature formula to compute the curvature at the point $P(\frac{2}{3},1,1).$
question.worked_solution:
The curvature $κ(t)$ is given by

$$
κ(t)=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}}.
$$

First, we find the value of $t$ that corresponds to the point $P(\frac{2}{3},1,1)$ on the given curve. We know that 

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =⟨\frac{2}{3},1,1⟩ \\ ⟨\frac{2{t}^{3}}{3},{t}^{2},\,\,t⟩ & =⟨\frac{2}{3},1,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the respective components gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2{t}^{3}}{3}=\frac{2}{3} \\ {t}^{2}=1 \\ t=1.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equality, $t=1.$ This value also satisfies the other two equations. Therefore, $P(\frac{2}{3},1,1)$ is at the tip of $r(1).$ 

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$, ${r}^{′}(1),$  and $‖{r}^{′}(1)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{2{t}^{3}}{3}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)⟩ \\  & =⟨2{t}^{2},\,2t,\,1⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(1) & =⟨2,2,1⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(1)‖ & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}}=3\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find ${r}^{″}(t)$ and ${r}^{″}(1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{″}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨4t,\,2,\,0⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(1) & =⟨4,2,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the cross-product and its magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(1)\times {r}^{″}(1) & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 2 & 1 \\ 4 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 4 & 0\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 4 & 2\end{aligned}|k \\  & =-2i+4j-4k \\ ‖{r}^{′}(1)\times {r}^{″}(1)‖ & =\sqrt{(-2)^{2}+{4}^{2}+(-4)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{36} \\  & =6\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the curvature at $t=1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(1) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(1)\times {r}^{″}(1)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(1){‖}^{3}} \\  & =\frac{6}{{3}^{3}} \\  & =\frac{2}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$
